observed_vs_claimed: CLAIMED: RELAX(n) >= 2^n for every n >= 1, and T_n >= 2^n. OBSERVED (explicit counters, one increment per directed edge scanned = the solution's own definition of a RELAX invocation, lines 0012-0013; no wall clock anywhere): RELAX(n) for n = 1..14 = 5, 12, 22, 35, 51, 70, 92, 117, 145, 176, 210, 247, 287, 330, matching the closed form (n+1)(3n+2)/2 exactly at every measured n -- i.e. Theta(n^2) with visible constants (leading coefficient 3/2), not Omega(2^n). The claimed bound is first violated at n = 7 (92 vs 128) and the gap widens monotonically: n=10 gives 176 vs 1024, n=14 gives 330 vs 16384. Per-vertex extraction counts give T_n = n+1 exactly for every n (2,3,4,...,15 for n=1..14), so the recurrence T_i >= 2 T_{i-1} (line 0072) and the induction T_n >= 2^n (line 0079) are false from n = 2 onward. The refutation is not an artifact of any under-specified detail: identical counts (92,117,145,176,210,247 at n=7..12) are produced under all 6 implemented readings of the queue/tie-breaking (Q as a multiset of re-inserted entries vs. a decrease-key vertex set; relaxing with current d[u] vs. the stale popped key; ties by smallest vs. largest topological index), and under every admissible value of the free parameter B (B = 2n+3, 4n+5, n^2+2n+3, 1000, 2^(n+2) all give exactly the same counts -- the count is B-independent). Strongest check: a brute-force oracle exhaustively maximises the RELAX count over EVERY legal execution of the specified algorithm (all min-key tie-breaking choices, DFS with memoisation over full (d, queue-multiset) states, search completed without truncation) for n = 1..7; the maximum equals the deterministic count exactly (5,12,22,35,51,70,92), so no tie-breaking discipline whatsoever attains 2^n. ROOT CAUSE: every indirect shortcut a_{i-1}->b_i->a_i improves a distance by exactly 1, and the solution's own invariant n >= -d[a_j] >= 0 (lines 0038-0039) then caps each a_j at n+1 extractions -- so the 'two a_i-extractions per i-epoch' lemma (lines 0053-0068) is inconsistent with the solution's own invariant. Mechanically, the first bullet of that lemma is where it breaks: the direct edge a_{i-1}->a_i produces NO strict decrease of d[a_i], because d[a_i] was already lowered to that value (or below) by the b-cascade of the previous epoch, so the guard 'd[v] > d[u]+w' is false and no re-insertion occurs. The G_5 trace confirms this: a_5 is extracted exactly at keys 0,-1,-2,-3,-4,-5 (6 = n+1 times) and final d[a_j] = -j.
faithfulness_notes: The solution fully specifies both the algorithm and the graph family, so the implementation is literal and nothing had to be invented. Graph: V, the edge set, the weights W_i = B^(n-i) with B an integer > 2n+2 (the solution's example B = 4n+5 is the primary setting; four other admissible B values are swept), and source a0 -- all built exactly as written in lines 0016-0027, and verified to be a DAG by checking that every edge goes forward in the solution's own stated topological order. Algorithm: d[s]=0, d[v]=+infinity otherwise (represented as None so no float ever enters the arithmetic), insert s; while Q nonempty extract a minimum-key vertex and scan every outgoing edge, applying 'if d[v] > d[u]+w(u,v) then d[v] <- d[u]+w(u,v) and (re)insert v' (line 0008). All weights, distances and counters are exact Python ints; no floating point is used and nothing is timed. Two details the prose leaves open were each implemented BOTH ways rather than chosen arbitrarily: (i) whether Q is a multiset of re-inserted entries (the literal '(re)insert v in Q') or a single keyed entry per vertex (the literal 'min-priority queue Q keyed by d[.]'), and (ii) whether a popped vertex is relaxed from its current d[u] (literal reading of line 0008) or from the key it was popped with. Tie-breaking is not specified at all, so besides two fixed deterministic rules an exhaustive oracle maximises the count over all tie-breaking choices. Oracles: exact shortest distances computed independently twice (topological-order DP and exhaustive enumeration of all directed paths from a0) agree with each other and with the simulated algorithm's final d[] for n = 1..6, confirming the simulation is a correct execution of the stated procedure; the operation-count oracle is the exhaustive over-all-executions maximiser described above. The run is fully deterministic -- no randomness and no seeds are involved.
